title: [CUDA Graph] Reduce memory by reusing a process-wide capture stream
body:
## Motivation

SGLang already uses a process-wide graph-private memory pool across CUDA graph runners. However, each default `graph_capture()` session previously created its own side stream. Sharing only the pool handle does not let the CUDA caching allocator reuse all compatible blocks when those allocations belong to different streams.

Tracked in #37113.

This PR reduces speculative decode overhead by reusing draft attention metadata across MTP draft steps.

## Problem

title: [Feat] Add fast EP scaling with NCCL communicator split
body:
## Purpose

The community-proposed [ElasticEP](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-05-14-elastic-expert-parallelism) flow scales an instance at runtime by creating/destroying Ray workers, rebuilding the stateless comm group, migrating and rearranging expert weights, and re-warming the compiled kernels. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite we measured ~31 s to scale up and ~7 s to scale down.

title: [V1][Perf] Cap detokenizer prompt-prime window for long prompts
body:
## Purpose

- `FastIncrementalDetokenizer` primes the `tokenizers` `DecodeStream` with the entire prompt (`DecodeStream(ids=request.prompt_token_ids)`). Priming is O(prompt_len) and runs lazily on the first output token's decode step, so for very long prompts it dominates first-token detokenization latency. Incremental decoding of output tokens only needs a short trailing window of prompt context, so this PR caps the primed ids to the last MAX_PROMPT_PRIME_TOKENS (128).

- The value of MAX_PROMPT_PRIME_TOKENS, 128, is a large-enough magic number for any BPE-merge / multi-byte span.
